claims.cards/assisted_pull_up.json#c1: Take the bar overhand, about shoulder width or a little wider, put the knees (or feet) on the pad and let body weight push it down until you hang with straight arms.
claims.cards/assisted_pull_up.json#c12: NSCA-editor textbook guidance is to perform all grips with the thumbs around the bar. Written for barbell lifts (a drill lifting a bar from the floor); applied to the assisted pull-up machine's bar by inference.
claims.cards/assisted_pull_up.json#c14: In 20 healthy adults squeezing a hand dynamometer, grip was strongest with the wrist in the position they chose themselves (about 35 degrees bent back) and weaker when the wrist was moved 10 to 15 degrees away from it in any direction, including curled forward (flexion). Applied to holding a bar or handle by reasoning, not measured on this exercise.
claims.cards/assisted_pull_up.json#grip.type: Overhand (pronated), palms away, full closed grip.
